To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of spatial inliers alone is not sufficient for discriminating relevant and irrelevant database photos and that geometric bursts, i. e. sets of visual elements that appear in similar geometric configurations, cause this problem.

(1) the number of inlier points found by spatial verification cannot be used as a proxy for the similarity between two images in large-scale location recognition, (2) geometric bursts are a major cause of this problem, (3) we propose algorithms for detecting bursts and handling them in a principled manner, and (4) using these algorithms leads to a significant improvement of the recall achievable at high precision in location recognition.
